subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Find the number of ways of selecting a cricket team of 11 players from 7 batsmen and 6 bowlers such that there will be at least 5 bowlers in the team.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.56 — SAQ chapter 9 Permutations & Combinations, answer 70. Printed appearances: TS 16, 18, 20 and AP 16. ⚠ THE 1+2+1 SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed anywhere in this unit's pages (SAQ book pp.55–58, VSAQ book pp.78–81 and Star Questions Plus book p.93 print none). recall_prompt: Say how you would count the teams — which compositions are allowed, how each is counted, and how you finish.
insider_note: "At least 5 bowlers" is exactly two cases here, 5 and 6, because only 6 bowlers exist. The case table carries its own mark, and the two case totals are added at the end, never multiplied.

steps.label: List the allowed compositions
steps.margin_note: First mark. There are only 6 bowlers, so "at least 5" means exactly 5 or exactly 6. The batsmen fill the rest of the 11.
lines: Team of 11 from 7 batsmen and 6 bowlers,
with at least 5 bowlers. Two cases:

recall.must_convey: That "at least 5 bowlers" gives exactly two cases — 5 bowlers with 6 batsmen, or 6 bowlers with 5 batsmen.
accept: at least five bowlers means five bowlers and six batsmen or six bowlers and five batsmen
two cases, five plus six or six plus five
there are only six bowlers so the cases are five bowlers or six bowlers
at least five ante five bowlers six batsmen leda six bowlers five batsmen, rendu cases
list the compositions, five and six or six and five

steps.why: A team with 5 bowlers and a team with 6 bowlers can never be the same team, so the cases do not overlap and can be added. Listing them first is what makes the addition legal.
common_mistakes: Reading "at least 5" as "exactly 5" and missing the second case.
Adding a case with 7 bowlers — there are only 6.

steps.label: Count each composition
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Each case is a choice of bowlers times a choice of batsmen — multiply within a case. ⁷C₅ = ⁷C₂ = 21 saves arithmetic.

recall.must_convey: That within each case the bowler choice and the batsman choice are multiplied — 6 C 5 times 7 C 6 is 42, and 6 C 6 times 7 C 5 is 21.
accept: six C five times seven C six is forty two and six C six times seven C five is twenty one
multiply the bowler selection by the batsman selection in each case, forty two and twenty one
case one gives forty two and case two gives twenty one
prathi case lo bowlers into batsmen multiply cheyali, forty two and twenty one
six times seven is forty two, one times twenty one is twenty one

steps.why: Inside one case the two choices are made together — every set of bowlers goes with every set of batsmen — so the counts multiply. Between cases the choices are alternatives, so they add.
common_mistakes: Adding ⁶C₅ and ⁷C₆ inside a case instead of multiplying.
Using ⁷P₆ or ⁷P₅ — a team is a selection, order does not matter.
Computing ⁷C₅ as 7·6·5/6 = 35 (that is ⁷C₃); ⁷C₅ = ⁷C₂ = 21.

steps.label: Add the cases
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The two cases are alternatives, so add them: 42 + 21 = 63.

recall.must_convey: That the two case counts are added to give 63.
accept: add the two cases forty two plus twenty one is sixty three
the cases are added to give sixty three ways
rendu cases add cheste sixty three
forty two and twenty one make sixty three

steps.why: Different compositions cannot be the same team, so no team is counted twice and the sum is the full count.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the cases (42 · 21) instead of adding.
Forgetting to add the second case and answering 42.
